app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Multiple services (frontend / frontend-proxy and callers) receive TCP connection refused when connecting to the product-catalog ClusterIP (10.96.210.204:8080). Traces show repeated errors “connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.210.204:8080” and gRPC UNAVAILABLE/failure to connect to all addresses. The product-catalog Service resolves to ClusterIP 10.96.210.204 and its Endpoint is the product-catalog Pod (10.244.1.15:8080), but TCP connects are refused — i.e., the product-catalog process in the pod is not accepting connections on the pod network interface (process not bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 or crashed between checks).

args.root_cause: Multiple services (frontend / frontend-proxy and callers) receive TCP connection refused when connecting to the product-catalog ClusterIP (10.96.210.204:8080). Traces show repeated errors “connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.210.204:8080” and gRPC UNAVAILABLE/failure to connect to all addresses. The product-catalog Service resolves to ClusterIP 10.96.210.204 and its Endpoint is the product-catalog Pod (10.244.1.15:8080), but TCP connects are refused — i.e., the product-catalog process in the pod is not accepting connections on the pod network interface (process not bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 or crashed between checks).
args.evidence_summary: 1) Traces (frontend-proxy) contain repeated errors: e.g. traceID=122187807ba1efa5d8f673c2bf731a5a: "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.210.204:8080"; several other traces show the same ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.210.204:8080 and one shows: "failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:10.96.210.204:8080: Failed to connect to remote host: Connection refused". 2) kubectl get services (astronomy-shop) shows product-catalog ClusterIP 10.96.210.204 (port 8080). 3) kubectl describe service/product-catalog shows Endpoints: 10.244.1.15:8080. 4) kubectl describe pod/product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-4vlbz shows the pod is Running and Ready and container port 8080 is declared. 5) frontend-proxy logs and traces show the failures originate when calling product-catalog. Together this shows DNS/Service routing is correct but TCP connect to product-catalog:8080 is refused.
args.investigation_summary: Steps taken: (1) Collected cluster inventory (pods & services) to see components in astronomy-shop. (2) Retrieved frontend-proxy logs to check for errors. (3) Retrieved error traces for frontend-proxy — observed repeated ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.210.204:8080. (4) Mapped the IP to a service by listing services (found product-catalog with ClusterIP 10.96.210.204). (5) Described the product-catalog Service (confirmed endpoints -> 10.244.1.15:8080) and product-catalog Pod (pod Running/Ready). Conclusion: networking and Service DNS resolve correctly, but product-catalog is refusing TCP connections (process not accepting connections on the pod interface).

evaluation.rca_motivation: Ground truth is a 10s latency/delay added by the edge proxy (Envoy) on image requests, with backend services healthy. The agent instead describes connection refusals to the product-catalog ClusterIP and a pod not accepting connections—this is a different component, different symptom (ECONNREFUSED vs added delay), and entirely wrong root cause.
